newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Bay developers to invest 145 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Manila Bay developers to invest 145 bln pesos.

text.p: Real estate developers in the Manila Bay reclamation project said they would initially invest at least 145 billion pesos over the next five years to develop the 1,500 hectare (3,705-acre) area into a modern city.

The amount is 24 percent of the 594.7 billion peso target investment of the government for 1993-1998 for its various infrastructure programmes on energy, transport, water, communications and social infrastructure combined, the developers said in a statement.

The developers of the area, which is called Boulevard 2000, were led by Amari Coastal and Development Corp, a joint venture by Centennial City and Ital-Thai Development Plc, and SM Inc, a unit of SM Development Corp.
"A 145 billion peso investment over the next five years will create jobs for at least 90,000 persons per year," the group said.
"Assuming an average annual income of 100,000 pesos, this means that the Boulevard 2000 will take care of addressing 3.8 percent (of) the annual employment target for the urban sector."
The developers issued the statement weeks after President Fidel Ramos ordered a review of all the contracts involved in the project.
An allegation by a senator that the contract to Amari Coastal was underpriced prompted the review. Amari has denied any wrongdoing.
